name: tutorial-interactive
description: Plays the Tutorial Pit the way a first-time player does: every step is driven by a real click on the control the tutorial card points at — speed button, toolbar, hire buttons, blast panel, event choices — and each beat waits for the tutorial's own rails to advance (waitForTutorialStep) before the next click, mirroring the retired playtest definition's click path (seismic survey at 23,23; the box cut dug down the west face before the drill grid; drill grid on the exact 20,20-30,30 rectangle; haul before deliver). Every tutorial-facing step is role-marked 'player' or 'setup' (issue #479): a player step's interaction may not fall back to a console command, so a step that cannot actually be clicked fails the scenario instead of passing on a typed shortcut.

steps.description: Setup: load Tutorial Pit — the level regenerates the terrain at its own size and re-frames the camera. #553: cash bumped from $80,000 to $250,000 -- drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action, so this file needs a driving_center/training/drill_rig it never used to, on top of the original manager/driver/hauler/warehouse shopping list. #555: bumped again to $320,000 -- dig_ramp_segment is now gated the same way, so this file also needs a driving.excavator course and a rock_digger ($52,500 together) plus the extra payroll/fuel/maintenance drain of the real ticks box-cut now spends actually digging instead of completing in the same tick it was ordered. #557: bumped again to $340,000 -- evacuateZone (Evacuation.ts) now genuinely routes the crew out to a reachable safe cell and back, instead of the previous no-op teleport, so the drill/charge/blast sequence spends real additional ticks (and payroll) on the walk; by build-storage this file's own `build freight_warehouse at:6,6` step was landing $9,182 short of the $15,000 cost (direct-traced, command mode) at the old $320,000 headroom.
Step time-speed: coach mark docked bottom-centre, speed button glowing, mine still visible

Command-mode-only unpause (issue #585): tutorial_start now genuinely sets isPaused (matches a real player's first view of the tutorial, paused so the card can be read) -- and tickCommand's own loop stops after exactly one real tick while paused regardless of the requested count, so every bare `tick N` below (training waits, haul waits) would silently advance only 1 tick without this. Interaction mode's own waitForTutorialStep steps drive their own real clock independent of console pause state, so this resume has no effect there.
time-speed complete: real click on the speed button cycles 1x to 2x, card advances to Hire Surveyor
Player follows the glowing Crew button — the tutorial card must not swallow the click
hire-surveyor complete: Hire clicked in the crew panel, surveyor appears on site

expect.note: The tutorial is on rails: leaving for the world map mid-step is how a player loses it, so that button must be inert while the tutorial is up (mirrors tutorial.json's hire-surveyor beat).

steps.description: Test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage: hiring already grants Rookie geology (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts, same for the UI hire button and this console command), so this only raises the level for tighter survey estimates. No role tag — there is no UI control for this and none should exist; the player-facing way to raise a skill is `employee train` at a training building, which this scenario does not need. Command mode keeps running it unchanged; interaction mode keeps it as an unmarked (legacy) command step.

the hired surveyor can actually be sent to survey: opening the Survey panel alone must already show a usable Run button — a surveyor who cannot survey is not a surveyor. If Run is disabled here, hiring grants no geology qualification and no button in the game grants one (mirrors tutorial.json's own standalone beat).

survey complete: seismic (the method the card names), target picked inside the step's outlined region (18..28), dispatched, and the surveyor walks out and works it. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock for the walk — no scripted `tick` needed once a click starts it.
hire-driller complete: driller hired through the crew panel

#681: build-living-quarters, click half -- the tutorial's new step 3a-i, placed right after hiring the driller and before the box-cut/drill-plan/charge/sequence stretch that used to run this crew unmanaged for ~400 ticks. A tier-1 living_quarters gives that stretch's forced rest somewhere real to send a collapsing employee. #556: ordering a building queues a construction site instead of placing it instantly -- this step only confirms the order landed (orderedBuildingCount increases); the wait step right below drives the site to completion the same way drill-plan/charge below it wait for holeCount/chargedCount.

#556/#816: build-living-quarters complete -- the driller or surveyor (both idle, no skill required for place_building) walks to (18,14) and builds the tier-1 living_quarters over its ~40-tick base duration. Waits on buildingCount itself rather than waitForTutorialStep, matching the drill-plan/charge waits below -- the tutorial card only flips to 'set-early-policy' once the building genuinely exists.

#681: set-early-policy complete -- the tutorial's new step 3a-ii. A living_quarters alone does not force anyone to rest: forceShiftRestIfNeededByPolicy (GameLoop.ts) only engages once state.sitePolicy.revision > 0, so this policy application is what actually makes the building above protect the crew through the grind that follows. Selects Continuous under Shift Mode first, then Apply -- shift_8h's own SHIFT_DURATIONS_TICKS (8) is shorter than a single drill_hole action, so applying it this early interrupted the queued vehicle-gated work below before it could finish (confirmed live pre-#700). Continuous still forces rest on hunger/fatigue (shouldForceRest checks that in every mode), just without the shift-length cap. The later set-policy step (unchanged) still teaches shift_8h once the grind is over. #707: timeout 15 -> 30 -- this was the only step in the file below the 30s floor every other player step uses; its `waitForTutorialStep` action's own inner deadline defaults to 30000ms (interaction-executor.ts) but effectiveStepTimeoutMs (scenario-utils.ts) doesn't know that action's `timeout` field (only `timeoutMs`/its own DEFAULT_INNER_TIMEOUT_MS table), so the outer 15000ms raced and lost first on a slow (no-GPU, #475) render -- confirmed live: the tutorial card had already reached 'build-driving-center' by the time the step's own 15s wall clock expired.

#553: build-driving-center, click half: driving_center ordered through the Build panel -- drill_hole became a queued, vehicle-gated action (a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole), and hiring only grants the driller their 'blasting' qualification, never the driving.drill_rig licence a drill_rig needs. This step and the two after it (train-driller, buy-drill-rig-assign) close that gap, the same deadlock class #552 fixed for hauling. #556/#816: ordering a building queues a construction site instead of placing it instantly, and `employee train` requires a REAL driving_center (state.buildings, not a pending order) -- confirmed via direct trace that training was genuinely refused immediately after this step with no wait in between, independent of the place_building livelock #816 also found and fixed. The wait step right below drives the site to completion before training is attempted, matching build-living-quarters/build-storage above.

#556/#816: build-driving-center complete -- the driving_center site finishes construction (root-cause livelock in place_building's dispatch/interruption logic fixed: an idle bystander employee standing on a just-completed building's footprint is now relocated the same way the builder already was, so a proactive-rest policy no longer strands anyone permanently).

#553: train-driller, click half: driving.drill_rig course booked at the driving_center just built. Training itself takes real ticks (TRAINING_BASE_TICKS, balance.ts) -- command mode has no implicit clock between steps (unlike interaction mode's own waitForTutorialStep), so the wait is its own step right below, mirroring this file's existing tick-1/tick-6 wait-only beats. #816: the driving_center order above now genuinely completes before this step runs (wait_until step inserted), and the root-cause place_building livelock (an idle bystander stranded on a just-completed building's footprint) is fixed in tickTaskCompletion.ts -- training succeeds for real, no longer declared refused.

#553: train-driller complete: the training course finishes and the driller (employee #2) is granted driving.drill_rig. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock in interaction mode; command mode needs the explicit tick since it has no implicit clock between steps.
buy-drill-rig-assign, first half: Vehicles panel open, tier-1 drill_rig bought and placed on the terrain surface

#555: train-digger, click half: driving.excavator course booked at the driving_center built above -- dig_ramp_segment work (the box-cut step below) now requires this licence + a rock_digger vehicle, the same gate #553 put on drilling. The surveyor (employee #1) is idle since the survey step completed, so they're who trains here. Training itself takes real ticks (TRAINING_BASE_TICKS, balance.ts) -- command mode has no implicit clock between steps, so the wait is its own step right below, mirroring train-driller's own click/wait split above. #816: no longer downstream of the set_policy mode:continuous construction livelock -- driving_center completes for real and place_building's root-cause livelock is fixed, so this succeeds genuinely.

#555: train-digger complete: the training course finishes and the surveyor (employee #1) is granted driving.excavator. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock in interaction mode; command mode needs the explicit tick since it has no implicit clock between steps.
buy-rock-digger-assign, first half: Vehicles panel open, tier-1 rock_digger bought and placed on the terrain surface

#555: buy-rock-digger-assign complete: Assign clicked, then the tutorial's own clock runs while the newly-licensed digger (employee #1) walks to the rock_digger and boards -- box-cut's own dig_ramp_segment work can only ever land a segment once this actually completes. #816: no longer downstream of the set_policy mode:continuous construction livelock -- driving_center completes for real and place_building's root-cause livelock is fixed, so this succeeds genuinely.

box-cut complete: dig the starter cut down the west face of the drill pattern before the first shot, so the blasted rock has a free face and a void to fall into (real open pits pioneer this access cut first). waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock — no scripted `tick` needed.

steps.description: Test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage — see the geology assign_skill step above for why this stays an unmarked (legacy) command step in interaction mode too.

#707: test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage — grants employee #1 (surveyor→digger, trained driving.excavator above) the blasting qualification. `charge_hole` gates on `requiredSkill: 'blasting'` alone (mining.ts) -- no vehicle or driving licence needed -- so employee #1, idle since box-cut finished, can now split the 9 `charge_hole` dispatches with the driller (employee #2) instead of the driller carrying drilling and all 9 charges alone. That single-employee grind is what let interaction mode's extra polling ticks (interaction-mode ticks run further ahead than command-mode ticks for the same step sequence) push well-being to 0 and hold it past REVOLT_TICKS (120 ticks, balance.ts), ending the level in a genuine worker_revolt moments before the blast step. Splitting the charge workload across two qualified employees shortens the real-tick span charging takes, closing that race. See the geology assign_skill step above for why this stays an unmarked (legacy) command step in interaction mode too.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:3 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: drill-plan, click half: grid tool dragged over the exact 20,20-26,26 rectangle the card asks for, confirmed. #553: this only orders the 9 holes -- drill_hole became a queued, vehicle-gated action, so holeCount stays 0 until the driller (equipped above) actually drives the drill_rig to each one. The wait is its own step right below. #554-followup (issue #586 CI, rounds 4-5): round 4 corrected the command from rows:3 cols:3 spacing:5 (9 holes) to rows:4 cols:4 spacing:3 (16 holes), reasoning the spacing stepper is unreachable this early in the rail (confirmed live, still true) so the declared spacing:5 could never be real. That was half right: spacing really is stuck at the tool's own DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3, but the drag rectangle producing 16 holes at that spacing was itself a latent bug in the region the tutorial rail snaps this drag to (REGION.drill, tutorialStages.ts), sized for a spacing of 5 that Drill.ts has never actually used since #479 -- nothing caught it because charging was instant until #553/#554, so the extra holes never cost real time. Round 5 fixes REGION.drill directly (20-30 -> 20-26), restoring the tutorial's originally-intended 3x3/9-hole workload for a lone early-tutorial employee with no living quarters yet; a 16-hole grid drove that same employee into a full worker revolt partway through charging (see the charging step's own note below). Command and drag corrected back in step to match the fixed region.

#553: drill-plan complete: the driller drives the drill_rig to all 9 ordered holes and drills them (sandbox-measured: a single driller/drill_rig lands a 3x3 spacing:3 grid on tutorial_pit comfortably inside 400 ticks door-to-door). #554-followup round 6 (issue #586 CI): previously used waitForTutorialStep(stepId:'charge'), which resolves the instant the FIRST hole lands (createComparisonStep's isComplete fires on the first increase past its snapshot -- 'drill-plan' advances to 'charge' after hole 1 of 9, not all 9). The very next step's `charge hole:*` order then only covered whatever was drilled AT THAT MOMENT -- usually just the one hole -- leaving the other 8 permanently uncharged (no later step re-issues the order), which is what left 'Auto Sequence' unreachable further down: charging never actually finished. Switched to waitUntil on holeCount itself so this step keeps waiting until every hole is actually down, in both modes, rather than stopping the moment the tutorial card first flips.

Defensive: a `tick N` step silently completes fewer ticks than requested if a random event fires mid-wait, and every subsequent tick then refuses until the event is resolved. No-op when nothing is pending.

charge ordered: Charge All Holes clicked — the panel applies its own form defaults and hole rows turn amber/loading (#554: charging is real work now, so the click only queues the order; the wait step right after drains it and confirms the tutorial advances to sequence once every hole has actually landed).

#554-followup round 6 (issue #586 CI): earlier rounds waited only for the FIRST charge to land (tutorialStep flips to 'sequence' the instant chargedCount first increases -- createComparisonStep's isComplete, same premature-advance behaviour as drill-plan above) and moved on with 8 of 9 holes still uncharged. That left 'Auto Sequence' unreachable further down the file: the sequence panel's own auto-sequence control only ever became reachable once every ordered charge had actually landed, so a scenario that stopped at chargedCount:1 could never proceed no matter how the following steps were reshuffled. Waiting for full completion here (chargedCount:9) is the real fix -- the drill-plan step above now also waits for all 9 holes before charging is ordered (round 6), so this order only ever targets the full 9 in the first place, unlike the partial orders earlier rounds were chasing. A 16-hole grid at this same lone-employee, no-living-quarters stage drove a full WORKER REVOLT at cumulative tick 318 (WorkerRevolt.ts's REVOLT_TICKS=120 sticky-zero window); REGION.drill (tutorialStages.ts) was fixed at the source to restore the tutorial's originally-intended 3x3/9-hole workload, which comfortably finishes charging well short of that threshold.
sequence complete: Auto Sequence clicked, delay labels appear on every hole. #557: the tutorial now advances to 'evacuate-zone' next, not straight to 'blast' -- the new step between them.

steps.command: zone clear x1:5 y1:5 x2:41 y2:41
steps.description: #557: evacuate-zone. computeDangerZone(state.drillHoles, BLAST_DANGER_MARGIN_M) for this exact 3x3/spacing:3 grid at (20,20) pads out to (5,5)-(41,41) -- on tutorial_pit's 32x32 map that covers nearly the whole site, so the driller (parked at the pattern they just finished charging) and the surveyor (idle since the survey step) are both still inside it. autoAdvance has kept the Blast Workshop on step 5 (Fire) since sequencing completed -- no tab click needed before Sound the Horn is reachable. Sound the Horn sends the same box this command declares (Fire.ts's soundHorn(), computed live). clearZone no longer teleports (#557): this only sets a destination for whoever is inside, so the wait_until step right after is what proves the walkout actually finished, not this click itself.

#557: drain the real walkout Sound the Horn just ordered -- the tutorial card only advances to 'blast' once dangerZoneClear genuinely reports true, matching the drill-plan/charge wait_until steps above.
blast complete: Execute clicked, confirm dialog answered, crater and fragments appear, Blast Report closed; the scores card then auto-advances into the scripted consultant event

expect.note: Close dismisses BlastReportModal, which auto-opens with the real report right after DETONATE; scores card auto-advances, so tutorialStep is checked in the next beat (mirrors tutorial.json's own choice not to assert it here). holeCount/chargedCount/sequencedCount resetting to 0 is checkable in both modes and goes beyond what the DOM-only playtest reference could prove.

steps.description: event-fire-resolve complete: the consultant dialog is answered through its own buttons, outcome read, then dismissed. #776: raised to 90s -- this and the following post-blast steps (blast at step 31 leaves a 994-fragment muck pile this scenario never fully clears) each pay for this file's own shots:["overview","birdseye"] (2 screenshot renders + a state dump) under software-rasterization cost; step 37 below already failed on shot-capture cost alone with its actual command succeeding, so raised to the file's own established 90s precedent (steps 31/39/41/42) rather than retuning each step individually.

hire-manager complete: manager hired now that the event is resolved. #776: raised from 30s to 60s -- this step lands right after the blast sequence (steps 24-31) when the scene is heaviest, and effectiveStepTimeoutMs's formula-correct 35000ms (30s declared vs innerMs+margin) proved empirically insufficient in two independent interaction-mode runs, both timing out at exactly 35000ms with the real hire + tutorial advance to contract-accept already having succeeded before the deadline fired. #776 follow-up: raised again to 90s -- floored with every other post-blast step to this file's own established 90s precedent (steps 31/39/41/42), covering this scenario's shots:["overview","birdseye"] render cost rather than retuning each step by hand. Card sequence follows tutorialSteps.ts’s reordered canonical order (#556/#817): contract-accept now sits after build-storage, so a contract’s deadline no longer starts while a construction site is still going up.

#816 retarget: the two new order-then-wait pairs inserted upstream of the blast (build-living-quarters/build-driving-center, #556 construction sites) push this step's own command-mode entry tick from 303 to 621 (direct trace, command mode, this fix) -- roughly the +250-300 real ticks those two waits themselves cost, on top of #816's own root-cause dispatch fix (relocating a bystander stranded on a just-completed building's footprint, and letting an idle employee fall through to the open pool when its own taskQueue holds one permanently-unreachable entry) actually letting driving_center/drilling/charging complete for real instead of livelocking forever. Direct-traced (command mode) that a rubble_disposal offer is continuously present in the pool from tick 622 through at least tick 1021 (400-tick scan) -- unlike the earlier #689/#707 rounds' narrower single-instance windows, every ~20-tick rotation in this range still carries a rubble_disposal slot, so this step no longer needs to land inside one specific instance's narrow window. Retargeted 420 -> 721 (100 ticks above the command-mode floor of 621) with max_ticks widened 140 -> 220 to also clear a materially larger interaction-mode entry tick than command mode's own 621 -- interaction mode's extra role:'player' polling ticks (waitForTutorialStep/waitForSelector loops command mode's plain `command` string never runs) were already ~100 ticks ahead of command mode at a similar point in earlier, shorter rounds of this file (#707 follow-up 2's own tick-370-vs-303 trace), and this file has grown since; not independently confirmed under a live interaction-mode run this round (no browser session in this fix pass) -- if interaction mode's own entry to this step is ever traced past 721, retarget upward the same way #689/#707/#707-followup-2 each did, using the continuous-presence property above rather than re-deriving a narrow window. REPLACED for #556: an absolute tickCount target cannot hold here — command mode and interaction mode enter this step hundreds of ticks apart (interaction mode runs polling ticks command mode never does), and `equals` only matches going forward, so any single number is either already behind one mode or out of reach of the other. What the step actually needs is in the note above: a rubble_disposal offer is continuously present through this range, not confined to one narrow window, so a short relative block that turns the pool once (REFRESH_INTERVAL 20 ticks, Contract.ts) buys it in either mode.

hire-driver complete: driver hired through the crew panel. #776: raised from 30s to 60s -- same shape as the hire-manager and contract-accept steps' own #776 fixes above: effectiveStepTimeoutMs's formula-correct ~35000ms (30s declared vs innerMs+margin) proved empirically insufficient in two independent interaction-mode runs, both timing out here with the real hire + tutorial advance to vehicle-buy-assign already having succeeded before the deadline fired. #776 follow-up: raised again to 90s -- floored with every other post-blast step to this file's own established 90s precedent (steps 31/39/41/42), covering this scenario's shots:["overview","birdseye"] render cost rather than retuning each step by hand. #816: no longer downstream of the set_policy mode:continuous construction livelock -- driving_center/freight_warehouse both complete for real and cash recovers on schedule now that place_building's root-cause livelock is fixed, so this succeeds genuinely. Opens the Crew panel with ensurePanel rather than a bare toolbar click (#556/#817): with contract-accept moved below build-storage, the step before this one is the manager hire and the panel is already open — the toolbar tab toggles, so a second click would close it, and the rail (which lights the last reachable control) makes that click inert.

Test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage — see the geology assign_skill step above; hiring already grants Rookie driving.truck, this only raises the level. Kept for command mode, which needs it for its own explicit `vehicle driver 1 4` to succeed identically. #776: raised to 90s -- confirmed the actual command succeeded and only the shot-capture cost (this scenario's shots:["overview","birdseye"]) exceeded the tight 30s default on this and the surrounding post-blast steps; floored to the file's own established 90s precedent (steps 31/39/41/42) instead of retuning each step individually. #816: no longer downstream of the set_policy mode:continuous construction livelock -- fixed at the root (tickTaskCompletion.ts), so this succeeds genuinely.

vehicle-buy-assign, first half: Vehicles panel open, tier-1 hauler bought and placed on the terrain surface. #776: raised to 90s -- post-blast step under this scenario's shots:["overview","birdseye"] render cost; floored to the file's own established 90s precedent (steps 31/39/41/42) alongside its neighbors rather than retuning individually. #816: no longer downstream of the set_policy mode:continuous construction livelock -- cash recovers on schedule now that place_building's root-cause livelock is fixed, so this succeeds genuinely.

contract-accept complete: Accept clicked on the offer this step's `command` names. #513/#581: elsewhere in this file's sibling scenarios the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-type]`/`[data-contract-material]` rather than a bare `.bs-contract-accept` (which resolves to whichever offered card leads the DOM), so a scoped click can't silently accept a different contract than the command names. #653 review round (Finding 2): this step used to stay unscoped, reasoning that tutorialStages.ts's own 'contract-accept' stage declares its live target as the bare `#bs-contract-panel .bs-contract-accept` and that scoping raced the offer pool's own refresh clock (REFRESH_INTERVAL=20 ticks, Contract.ts) -- but an unscoped click accepts whichever offer leads the DOM, which is only rubble_disposal at some tick landings and a different type at others (replay-verified at varied timing), silently accepting the wrong contract while the later deliver step (scoped to `[data-contract-type="rubble_disposal"]`) then finds nothing to deliver and times out. Scoped now, matching contract-negotiation.json/contract-panel-visual.json's own accept steps: a `waitForSelector` on the scoped selector ahead of the click gives the refresh cycle time to surface the right card instead of assuming it's there instantly, and `expect.equals` on `activeContractCount` proves the right contract landed rather than merely some contract. #653: retargeted from `type:ore_sale material:gloomium` to `type:rubble_disposal` (no `material:` -- rubble_disposal contracts carry `materialId: ''`), because the ore_sale/gloomium contract this step used to accept could never actually be delivered later (see the deliver step's own note below) -- the debris hauler this tutorial buys only ever fills storage with excavation spoil, never an ore-bearing fragment. rubble_disposal is fulfilled by `consumeStoredOre()` drawing on raw `storedMassKg`, which the hauler does fill, making this the first contract type in this run the later deliver step can genuinely complete. Live-verified landing under real render load is ~100 extra ticks reaching this point (tick 332 vs command mode's tick 232), not the 300+ an earlier round of this file assumed. issue #585 (merge, agrees independently): a hardcoded id here is exactly as fragile as the DOM-scoped click above and for the same reason -- the contract pool's ids increment off total elapsed ticks (Contract.ts) -- reaching the same `type:rubble_disposal` selector via a separate trace before #653 landed. #776: raised from 30s to 60s -- this step lands right after the blast/event/hire-manager stretch above, and effectiveStepTimeoutMs's formula-correct ~35000ms (30s declared vs innerMs+margin) proved empirically insufficient in two independent interaction-mode runs, both timing out here with the real accept + tutorial advance to hire-driver already having succeeded before the deadline fired -- same shape as the hire-manager step's own #776 fix above. #776 follow-up: raised again to 90s -- floored with every other post-blast step to this file's own established 90s precedent (steps 31/39/41/42), covering this scenario's shots:["overview","birdseye"] render cost rather than retuning each step by hand.
